arxiv-2305-06153.title: Quantum Computing with dartboards
arxiv-2305-06153.creator: Ishaan Ganti, Srinivasan S. Iyengar
arxiv-2305-06153.description: Abstract We present a physically appealing and elegant picture for quantum computing using rules constructed for a game of darts. A dartboard is used to represent the state space in quantum mechanics and the act of throwing the dart is shown to have close similarities to the concept of measurement, or collapse of the wavefunction in quantum mechanics.

arxiv-2309-17142.title: Stirling complexes
arxiv-2309-17142.creator: Dmitry N. Kozlov with an appendix by Roy Meshulam
arxiv-2309-17142.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Dmitry N. Kozlov with an appendix by Roy Meshulam. In this paper we study natural reconfiguration spaces associated to the problem of distributing a fixed number of resources to labeled nodes of a tree network, so that no node is left empty. These spaces turn out to be cubical complexes, which can be thought of as higher-dimensional geometric extensions of the combinatorial Stirling problem of partitioning a set of named objects into non-empty labeled parts.

arxiv-2408-03480.title: Advancing EEG-Based Gaze Prediction Using Depthwise Separable Convolution and Enhanced Pre-Processing
arxiv-2408-03480.creator: Matthew L Key *, Tural Mehtiyev *, Xiaodong Qu
arxiv-2408-03480.description: Abstract In the field of EEG-based gaze prediction, the application of deep learning to interpret complex neural data poses significant challenges. This study evaluates the effectiveness of pre-processing techniques and the effect of additional depthwise separable convolution on EEG vision transformers (ViTs) in a pretrained model architecture.

arxiv-2409-16609.title: Random Forest Regression Feature Importance for Climate Impact Pathway Detection Journal: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
arxiv-2409-16609.creator: Meredith G. L. Brown, Matt Peterson, Irina Tezaur, Kara Peterson, Diana Bull
arxiv-2409-16609.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Meredith G. L. Brown, Matt Peterson, Irina Tezaur, Kara Peterson, Diana Bull. Disturbances to the climate system, both natural and anthropogenic, have far reaching impacts that are not always easy to identify or quantify using traditional climate science analyses or causal modeling techniques. In this paper, we develop a novel technique for discovering and ranking the chain of spatio-temporal downstream impacts of a climate source, referred to herein as a source-impact pathway, using Random Forest Regression (RFR) and SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) feature importances.

arxiv-2410-23957.title: Progress on Holographic Vacuum Misalignment
arxiv-2410-23957.creator: Maurizio Piai
arxiv-2410-23957.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Maurizio Piai. We summarise highlights from an ongoing research programme that aims, in the long run, at the ambitious goal of building a realistic, complete holographic composite-Higgs model. This contribution focuses on vacuum misalignment, by showing how to unify its description, as a phenomenon arising from weak coupling considerations, in the holographic description of a strongly coupled field theory in terms of a dual gravity theory. This is achieved by a non-trivial treatment of boundary-localised terms in the gravity action.

arxiv-2511-21726.title: Goal-Directed Search Outperforms Goal-Agnostic Memory Compression in Long-Context Memory Tasks
arxiv-2511-21726.creator: Yicong Zheng, Kevin L. McKee, Thomas Miconi, Zacharie Bugaud, Mick van Gelderen, Jed McCaleb
arxiv-2511-21726.description: Abstract How to enable human-like long-term memory in large language models (LLMs) has been a central question for unlocking more general capabilities such as few-shot generalization. Existing memory frameworks and benchmarks focus on finding the optimal memory compression algorithm for higher performance in tasks that require recollection and sometimes further reasoning.

pmc-12506860.title: Suppression of Elastic Scattering of CH4 by Graphene Passivation of Ni(111)
pmc-12506860.creator: Amjad Al Taleb, Francesc Viñes, Daniel Farías
pmc-12506860.description: We report high-resolution angular diffraction measurements of CH4 and Ne from Ni(111) and from a graphene (Gr) layer grown on Ni(111), whose effective atomic mass is enhanced by the strong Gr–Ni interaction. pmc-13328157.title: Home range size and foraging niche predict lead exposure variability in terrestrial birds
pmc-13328157.creator: Max M Gillings, Riccardo Ton, Simon C Griffith
pmc-13328157.description: Ecological risk assessments estimate chemical exposures in wildlife from contaminant concentrations within their surrounding environment. This approach precludes a detailed understanding of interactions between biota and contaminant sources. It also overlooks how the uneven and irregular use of space by animals influences variability in exposure.

pmc-13547530.title: Drone-delivered automated external defibrillators in prehospital emergency care: implementation evidence, bottlenecks, and conceptual integration with artificial intelligence and next-generation communications
pmc-13547530.creator: Hua Li, Yunxiao Zhao, Wenkai Guo, Ning Luo, Pu Li, Hang Liu, Kunpeng Yang, Wenjuan Sun, Bao Wang, Dong Li
pmc-13547530.description: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a major global health challenge. Survival depends on immediate cardiopulmonary resuscitation and early defibrillation. Static public-access defibrillator programs often fail to reach private, rural, or otherwise underserved locations. Drone-delivered automated external defibrillators (AEDs) may overcome ground-traffic and geographic barriers, but rapid delivery does not always lead to timely treatment.

pmc-13654940.title: Proteomic maps of synapses and synaptic vesicles across the central and enteric nervous systems
pmc-13654940.creator: Shiqi Liu, Qiwang Huang, Zhiwei Tu, Hao Shen, Guibin Wang, Huanjiao Jing, Yaoyao Bian, Xulian Cui, Linshuai Cui, Jian Wang, Chenxi Jia
pmc-13654940.description: While the synaptic proteome of the central nervous system (CNS) has been extensively characterized, its composition in the peripheral nervous system (PNS) remains unknown. There is an urgent need to delineate the precise proteomic landscape of the enteric nervous system (ENS), often referred to as the “second brain,” and to systematically compare its molecular heterogeneity with that of the CNS.

pmc-13656472.title: Interparental conflict and children’s sleep quality in the chinese family context: the serial mediating roles of emotional insecurity and subjective well-being
pmc-13656472.creator: Hongxia Hou, Yaxin Guan, Tiantian Luo
pmc-13656472.description: BackgroundSleep problems in children are an important risk factor for cognitive, emotional, and behavioral development. Previous studies have shown that interparental conflict is closely associated with poorer sleep quality in children. However, the internal psychological variables involved in this association, particularly how they may be understood within the Chinese family context, remain insufficiently examined.

uslaw-usc-t25-s393.title: 25 U.S.C. § 393 — Leases of restricted allotments
uslaw-usc-t25-s393.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t25-s393.description: United States Code, Title 25 (Indians); Chapter 12 (Lease, Sale, Or Surrender Of Allotted Or Unallotted Lands). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The restricted allotment of any Indian may be leased for farming and grazing purposes by the allottee or his heirs, subject only to the approval of the superintendent or other officer in charge of the reservation where the land is.
